title: That's why, and still: deshalb and trotzdem (Deshalb bin ich müde)
summary: deshalb gives the result, trotzdem says 'still, anyway'. Both take position 1, so the verb comes right after them. A whole weil part can take position 1 too. Plus: how do you feel, and why?
goals: Say what follows with deshalb: Ich arbeite viel. Deshalb bin ich oft müde.
Start with a weil part: Weil es regnet, nehmen wir den Bus.
Say how you feel and why: froh, nervös, sauer, zufrieden

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A2, chapter 5: So stressful! (Das hört sich gut an!)

sections.title: deshalb: that's why
sections.text:
[[weil]] gives the reason. [[deshalb]] gives the result:
- [[Ich bin müde, weil ich viel arbeite.]] (the reason)
- [[Ich arbeite viel. Deshalb bin ich müde.]] (the result)

[[deshalb]] takes **position 1**, so the verb comes right after it, then the subject. It's the rule from Unit 1: the verb is always second, as in [[In München wohne ich.]] [[deshalb]] can also go after the verb: [[Ich bin deshalb müde.]]

sections.title: trotzdem: still, anyway
sections.text:
[[trotzdem]] says that something happens **even though** there's a reason against it:
- [[Es regnet. Trotzdem gehen wir spazieren.]] = It's raining. We're going for a walk anyway.
- [[Ich war müde. Trotzdem bin ich zum Training gegangen.]] = I was tired. Still, I went to training.

The word order is the same as with [[deshalb]]: position 1 and the verb next, or after the verb: [[Wir gehen trotzdem spazieren.]]

[[spazieren gehen]] = to go for a walk; [[der Spaziergang]] = a walk.

sections.title: Result, or 'anyway'?
rows: I work a lot. That's why I'm often tired.
Deshalb bin ich zu spät gekommen.
The bus was late. That's why I was late.
I've got the day off. That's why I'm so glad.
It's raining. We're going for a walk anyway.
I was ill. Still, I worked.

sections.text: Russian поэтому doesn't move the verb: поэтому я устал. German [[deshalb]] does: [[Deshalb bin ich müde.]] The verb jumps in front of the subject. [[trotzdem]] is like всё равно, and it moves the verb too: [[Trotzdem gehen wir spazieren.]]

sections.title: The verb comes next
sections.text: After [[deshalb]] or [[trotzdem]] in position 1 comes the verb, not the subject: [[Deshalb bin ich müde]], not 'Deshalb ich bin müde'. This is the mistake Russian and English speakers make most.

sections.title: A whole weil part in position 1
sections.text:
Position 1 can even hold a whole [[weil]] part. Then the main verb comes right after the comma, so two verbs meet:
- [[Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause.]]
- [[Weil es regnet, nehmen wir den Bus.]]
- [[Weil der Kurs um neun anfängt, stehe ich um sieben auf.]]

sections.title: also means 'so', not 'also'
sections.text:
In speech you'll often hear [[also]] instead of [[deshalb]]: [[Ich habe heute Zeit, also kann ich dir helfen.]] It works the same way: the verb comes next.

At the start, with a comma, [[also]] is just 'well' or 'so': [[Also, ich finde das gut.]] And English 'also' is [[auch]].

sections.title: How do you feel?
sections.text:
Nicos Weg A2, chapter 5 asks how people feel. At A2 you can say more than [[gut]], and say why:
- [[Ich bin froh, weil ich heute frei habe.]] ([[froh]] = glad)
- [[Ich bin nervös, weil ich morgen eine Prüfung habe.]]
- [[Ich bin traurig, weil meine Freundin jetzt in Berlin wohnt.]] ([[traurig]] = sad)
- [[Ich bin sauer, weil Thomas schon wieder zu spät kommt.]] ([[sauer]] = sour, and in speech: annoyed)
- [[Ich bin zufrieden, weil ich viel geschafft habe.]] ([[zufrieden]] = satisfied)
- [[Ich habe Angst, weil der Verkehr so gefährlich ist.]] ([[die Angst]] = fear)

Short ones: [[Ich bin noch nicht wach.]] (awake) [[Heute bin ich faul.]] (lazy) [[Das ist nicht so schlimm.]] (bad, serious)

sections.title: Sport and rest
sections.text:
- [[Ich mache viel Sport, deshalb bin ich fit.]]
- [[Thomas ist nicht sehr sportlich. Trotzdem joggt er jeden Morgen.]] ([[sportlich]] = sporty)
- [[Nach der Arbeit brauche ich Ruhe.]] ([[die Ruhe]] = quiet, rest)
- [[Am Sonntag machen wir einen Spaziergang.]]
- [[Es regnet, und ich habe keinen Schirm. Jetzt bin ich nass.]] ([[nass]] = wet)

items.en: I work a lot. That's why I'm often tired.

items.en: I'm nervous because I have an exam tomorrow.

items.en: The train was late, so I missed the appointment.

items.en: I was tired, but I still went to training.

items.de: Ich habe heute Zeit, also kann ich dir helfen.
items.en: I've got time today, so I can help you.
We're going for a walk anyway.

items.de: Weil es regnet, nehmen wir den Bus.
items.en: Because it's raining, we're taking the bus.

items.de: Ich bin sauer, weil Thomas schon wieder zu spät kommt.
items.en: I'm annoyed because Thomas is late again.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I worked a lot. That's why I'm tired.
items.text: Ich habe viel gearbeitet. Deshalb ___ ich müde.
items.explanation: deshalb takes position 1, so the verb comes next and the subject after it: Deshalb bin ich müde.

items.question: Ich war krank. ___ bin ich zur Arbeit gegangen.
items.explanation: Being ill is a reason against going to work, and you went anyway: trotzdem. deshalb would mean that being ill was the reason for going. After weil the verb would go to the end.

items.prompt: (I was tired.) Still, I went to training.
answers: Trotzdem bin ich zum Training gegangen
Ich bin trotzdem zum Training gegangen
Zum Training bin ich trotzdem gegangen
items.explanation: trotzdem in position 1, then the verb: Trotzdem bin ich ... gegangen. Or after the verb: Ich bin trotzdem zum Training gegangen.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: Because the weather is nice, we're going by bike.
items.text: Weil das Wetter schön ist, ___ wir mit dem Rad.
items.explanation: The weil part is position 1, so the main verb comes right after the comma: Weil das Wetter schön ist, fahren wir mit dem Rad.

items.audio: Ich bin heute sehr nervös, weil ich am Nachmittag eine Prüfung habe.
items.question: Why is the person nervous?
items.explanation: weil ich am Nachmittag eine Prüfung habe = because I have an exam in the afternoon. nervös = nervous.
